code: library(magrittr) set.seed(20261017) data <- gss7677[gss7677$COHORT == "YOUNG", ] stat2 <- slca(status(2) ~ PAPRES + PADEG + MADEG) %>%    estimate(data = data, control = list(verbose = FALSE)) stat3 <- slca(status(3) ~ PAPRES + PADEG + MADEG) %>%    estimate(data = data, control = list(verbose = FALSE)) stat4 <- slca(status(4) ~ PAPRES + PADEG + MADEG) %>%    estimate(data = data, control = list(verbose = FALSE))  gof(stat2, stat3, stat4) #> Analysis of Goodness of Fit Table #>  #>       Df  logLik    AIC    BIC     Gsq Res. Df #> stat2 21 -1179.2 2400.4 2489.0 115.980      53 #> stat3 32 -1139.3 2342.6 2477.7  36.204      42 #> stat4 43 -1135.4 2356.8 2538.3  28.424      31 gof(stat2, stat3, stat4, test = "chisq") #> Analysis of Goodness of Fit Table #>  #>       Df  logLik    AIC    BIC     Gsq Res. Df Pr(>Chi)     #> stat2 21 -1179.2 2400.4 2489.0 115.980      53 1.34e-06 *** #> stat3 32 -1139.3 2342.6 2477.7  36.204      42   0.7225     #> stat4 43 -1135.4 2356.8 2538.3  28.424      31   0.5992     #> --- #> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1 # \donttest{ # Five replicates illustrate the interface only; use more for inference. absolute_boot <- gof(stat2, stat3, stat4, test = "boot",                      nboot = 5, maxiter = 5000, tol = 1e-6) absolute_boot #> Analysis of Goodness of Fit Table #>  #>       Df  logLik    AIC    BIC     Gsq Res. Df Pr(Boot) #> stat2 21 -1179.2 2400.4 2489.0 115.980      53   0.1667 #> stat3 32 -1139.3 2342.6 2477.7  36.204      42   0.1667 #> stat4 43 -1135.4 2356.8 2538.3  28.424      31   0.5000 attr(absolute_boot, "bootFail") #> stat2 stat3 stat4  #>     0     0     0  # }  compare(stat3, stat4) #> Analysis of Relative Model Fit #>  #> Model H0: stat3 #> Model H1: stat4 #>       Df  logLik    AIC    BIC    Gsq Res. Df #> stat3 32 -1139.3 2342.6 2477.7                #> stat4 43 -1135.4 2356.8 2538.3 7.7805      11 compare(stat3, stat4, test = "chisq") #> Analysis of Relative Model Fit #>  #> Model H0: stat3 #> Model H1: stat4 #>       Df  logLik    AIC    BIC    Gsq Res. Df Pr(>Chi) #> stat3 32 -1139.3 2342.6 2477.7                         #> stat4 43 -1135.4 2356.8 2538.3 7.7805      11   0.7328 # \donttest{ # Use EM refits here; always inspect convergence failures. relative_boot <- compare(stat3, stat4, test = "boot", method = "em",                          nboot = 5, maxiter = 5000, tol = 1e-6) relative_boot #> Analysis of Relative Model Fit #>  #> Model H0: stat3 #> Model H1: stat4 #>       Df  logLik    AIC    BIC    Gsq Res. Df Pr(Boot) #> stat3 32 -1139.3 2342.6 2477.7                         #> stat4 43 -1135.4 2356.8 2538.3 7.7805      11      0.5 attr(relative_boot, "bootFail") #> [1] 0 # }

what: Goodness-of-Fit Test for Fitted slca Model — gof
title: Goodness-of-Fit Test for Fitted slca Model — gof
text: Computes AIC, BIC, deviance statistic (G-squared) assessing goodness--fit fitted slca model. test argument specified, absolute model fit can evaluated using deviance statistics.

title: Goodness-of-Fit Test for Fitted slca Model — gof
code: gof(object, ...)  # S3 method for class 'slcafit' gof(    object, ..., test = c("none", "chisq", "boot"),    nboot = 100, plot = FALSE,    maxiter = 5000, tol = 1e-6, verbose = FALSE )  # S3 method for class 'slcafit' gof(   object,   ...,   test = c("none", "chisq", "boot"),   nboot = 100,   plot = FALSE,   maxiter = 5000,   tol = 1e-06,   verbose = FALSE )

title: Goodness-of-Fit Test for Fitted slca Model — gof
text: object object class slcafit, list slcafit objects. List names used model labels; unnamed elements labeled [[1]], [[2]], . ... additional objects class slcafit comparison. test character string specifying type test conducted. "chisq", chi-squared test conducted. "boot", bootstrap test conducted. nboot positive number specifying number bootstrap rounds performed. Non-integer values rounded . plot logical value indicating whether print histogram G-squared statistics boostrap samples, test = "boot". default FALSE. maxiter integer specifying maximum number iterations allowed estimation process bootstrap iteration. default 5000. tol numeric value specifying convergence tolerance bootstrap iteration. default 1e-6. verbose logical value indicating whether print progress updates number bootstrapping rounds completed.

title: Goodness-of-Fit Test for Fitted slca Model — gof
text: data.frame containing number parameters (Df), loglikelihood, AIC, BIC, G-squared statistics, residual degree freedom object. statistical test performed (using test), result includes corresponding p-value. test = "boot", failed bootstrap replicates omitted p-value calculation recorded bootFail, boot.fail.msgs, boot..msgs attributes. Absolute bootstrap samples retain fitted data's missing-value pattern. Nonconverged refits counted failures. \(B\) successful replicates \(b\) statistics least large observed, bootstrap p-value \((b + 1)/(B + 1)\).

title: Goodness-of-Fit Test for Fitted slca Model — gof
code: library(magrittr) set.seed(20261017) data <- gss7677[gss7677$COHORT == "YOUNG", ] stat2 <- slca(status(2) ~ PAPRES + PADEG + MADEG) %>%    estimate(data = data, control = list(verbose = FALSE)) stat3 <- slca(status(3) ~ PAPRES + PADEG + MADEG) %>%    estimate(data = data, control = list(verbose = FALSE)) stat4 <- slca(status(4) ~ PAPRES + PADEG + MADEG) %>%    estimate(data = data, control = list(verbose = FALSE))  gof(stat2, stat3, stat4) #> Analysis of Goodness of Fit Table #>  #>       Df  logLik    AIC    BIC     Gsq Res. Df #> stat2 21 -1179.2 2400.4 2489.0 115.980      53 #> stat3 32 -1139.3 2342.6 2477.7  36.204      42 #> stat4 43 -1135.4 2356.8 2538.3  28.424      31 gof(stat2, stat3, stat4, test = "chisq") #> Analysis of Goodness of Fit Table #>  #>       Df  logLik    AIC    BIC     Gsq Res. Df Pr(>Chi)     #> stat2 21 -1179.2 2400.4 2489.0 115.980      53 1.34e-06 *** #> stat3 32 -1139.3 2342.6 2477.7  36.204      42   0.7225     #> stat4 43 -1135.4 2356.8 2538.3  28.424      31   0.5992     #> --- #> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1 # \donttest{ # Five replicates illustrate the interface only; use more for inference. absolute_boot <- gof(stat2, stat3, stat4, test = "boot",                      nboot = 5, maxiter = 5000, tol = 1e-6) absolute_boot #> Analysis of Goodness of Fit Table #>  #>       Df  logLik    AIC    BIC     Gsq Res. Df Pr(Boot) #> stat2 21 -1179.2 2400.4 2489.0 115.980      53   0.1667 #> stat3 32 -1139.3 2342.6 2477.7  36.204      42   0.1667 #> stat4 43 -1135.4 2356.8 2538.3  28.424      31   0.5000 attr(absolute_boot, "bootFail") #> stat2 stat3 stat4  #>     0     0     0  # }  compare(stat3, stat4) #> Analysis of Relative Model Fit #>  #> Model H0: stat3 #> Model H1: stat4 #>       Df  logLik    AIC    BIC    Gsq Res. Df #> stat3 32 -1139.3 2342.6 2477.7                #> stat4 43 -1135.4 2356.8 2538.3 7.7805      11 compare(stat3, stat4, test = "chisq") #> Analysis of Relative Model Fit #>  #> Model H0: stat3 #> Model H1: stat4 #>       Df  logLik    AIC    BIC    Gsq Res. title: GSS 1976-1977 Data on Social Status and Tolerance towards Minorities — gss7677
text: dataset contains responses General Social Survey (GSS) years 1976 1977, focusing social status tolerance towards minorities. dataset can used replicate analyses conducted McCutcheon (1985) Bakk et al. (2014).  includes covariates interview year, age, sex, race, education level, income. Social status-related variables include father's occupation education level, well mother's education level. Tolerance towards minorities measured agreement three questions: (1) allowing public speaking, (2) allowing teaching, (3) allowing literature publication.

Latent transition analysis (LTA) slca(lx[3] ~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4,      ly[2] ~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4,      lx ~ ly) #> Structural Latent Variable Model #>  #> Latent variables (Root*):               #>  Label: lx* ly #> nclass: 3   2  #>  #> Measurement model:                             #>  lx -> { x1, x2, x3, x4 }  a #>  ly -> { y1, y2, y3, y4 }  b #>  #> Structural model:              #>  lx -> { ly } #>  #> Dependency constraints: #>  A        #>  lx -> ly # LTA with measurement invariance slca(l1[3] ~ y11 + y21 + y31 + y41,      l2[3] ~ y12 + y22 + y32 + y42,      l1 ~ l2, constraints = c("l1", "l2")) #> Structural Latent Variable Model #>  #> Latent variables (Root*):               #>  Label: l1* l2 #> nclass: 3   3  #>  #> Measurement model:                                 #>  l1 -> { y11, y21, y31, y41 }  a #>  l2 -> { y12, y22, y32, y42 }  a #>  #> Structural model:              #>  l1 -> { l2 } #>  #> Dependency constraints: #>  A        #>  l1 -> l2 # Joint latent class analysis slca(lx[2] ~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4,      ly[3] ~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4,      lz[2] ~ z1 + z2 + z3 + z4,      jc[3] ~ lx + ly + lz) #> Structural Latent Variable Model #>  #> Latent variables (Root*):                     #>  Label: lx ly lz jc* #> nclass: 2  3  2  3   #>  #> Measurement model:                             #>  lx -> { x1, x2, x3, x4 }  a #>  ly -> { y1, y2, y3, y4 }  b #>  lz -> { z1, z2, z3, z4 }  c #>  #> Structural model:                      #>  jc -> { lx, ly, lz } #>  #> Dependency constraints: #>  A        B        C        #>  jc -> lx jc -> ly jc -> lz #
